It is well known that the conventional electrode fabrication procedure for lithium ion batteries, such as slurry coating on metallic foil, is carefully carried out to achieve a good contact between electrode and current collector. From this point of view, we can understand that the contact resistance between the powder-compacted electrode layer, and the current collecting layer (stainless steel rod used in the present work), is also critical for cell performance.
